claim: VCO frequency-vs-VDD supply-pushing characterization for design/vco/vco_ring5.sch (the standalone current-starved 5-stage ring VCO, issue #24), measured open-loop with VCTRL held FIXED at four operating points (0.8, 0.9, 1.2, 1.5 V) spanning the 0.8-1.6 V free-running range sim/vco/records/20260904-163130-f3ae976.md characterizes, while VDD is the swept quantity (spec/target-spec.md row 1's ratified 1.80 V +/- 10 % range: 1.62, 1.80, 1.98 V, applied by the corner runner's own supply axis). It is the sibling of sim/vco: same DUT, same open-loop harness, same reducer, opposite independent variable -- sim/vco sweeps VCTRL at fixed VDD to characterize Kvco (MHz/V); this manifest holds VCTRL fixed and sweeps VDD to characterize fractional-frequency pushing (%/V). Its purpose is the first of the two prerequisites spec/decision-records/DR-006-statistical-rows-ratification.md names for a future ratification of row 13 Budget 1 (the AC supply-ripple limit): a sky130 supply-pushing measurement to replace the 1.67x realized-over-floor ratio DR-006 could only borrow from gf180-pll. It is measured design input, not a spec claim, and it ratifies nothing -- per CLAUDE.md, ratification is a separate decision-record act argued on its own merits, and DR-006 itself is merged and unedited. The PVT grid is the DR-003-ratified sky130 5-corner set (tt/ff/ss/sf/fs x -40/27/125 degC) crossed with row 1's ratified supply range; a given record's own **Corner matrix run** field states whether it covers that full 45-point grid or a declared subset, per sim/README.md's subset-justification rule.
spec_rows_note: spec/target-spec.md row 13 (supply sensitivity). Row 13 is DRAFT *by explicit decision* (DR-006, #151), not by omission, and this manifest does not change that: it measures the quantity DR-006's own Budget 1 discussion is written in -- fractional-frequency pushing of the ring, |df/f| per volt of VDD -- so that a future decision record arguing row 13 has a sky130 number to argue from instead of gf180-pll's borrowed 1.67x realized-over-floor ratio. Row 5 (Kvco) is deliberately NOT cited here: VCTRL is held fixed, so this manifest measures no tuning slope; sim/vco is the record that bears on row 5.
methodology_note: this testbench's DUT is design/vco/vco_ring5.sch driven open-loop (no PFD, charge pump, loop filter or divider in the path) -- it characterizes the VCO block alone, exactly as sim/vco does, and says nothing about the assembled loop's in-lock rail rejection, which is a separate transient campaign (issue #166). VCTRL is held FIXED at each of four operating points (0.8, 0.9, 1.2, 1.5 V) and the supply is the measured independent variable, supplied by the corner runner's own 1.62/1.80/1.98 V axis: the frequency-vs-VDD pushing figure is therefore a CROSS-POINT derivation over the three supply rows that share a (corner, temperature, VCTRL) triple, not a within-point slope, and the harness's own per-point tuning-summary table (which reports MHz per volt of the swept VCTRL axis) is not that figure -- see sim/vco-supply-pushing/analysis/pushing.py, which derives it from the record's own swept-axis table and appends it to the record at mint time. All four VCTRL values sit inside the free-running span sim/vco/records/20260904-163130-f3ae976.md measured (all 45 of its points oscillated at all six of its swept values), so unlike sim/vco -- a characterization sweep that deliberately runs past the edge of the tuning range, where a dead swept value is data -- a dead swept value here would leave a (corner, temperature, VCTRL) triple with no pushing figure at all: min_oscillating_points is therefore the full 4, and a non-oscillating swept value fails its point. The four values are chosen to resolve the pushing figure as a function of bias rather than report one number smuggled out of a single operating point, because the two mechanisms that set it have OPPOSITE signs and their sum changes sign inside this range. 0.8 V is the bottom of the characterized tuning range, where the starving branch is weakest and closest to the supply-independent-current idealization DR-006's `1/VDD` floor argument assumes; 0.9 V is the operating point nearest the closed-loop target (sim/pll-lock drives N=25 against a 10 MHz reference for 250 MHz, and sim/vco measured 318.1 MHz at tt/27 degC/1.80 V/VCTRL=0.9 V, the characterized point closest to that target); 1.2 V and 1.5 V walk the current-dominated upper half of the usable span, where the sum has flipped sign, with 1.5 V carrying the largest pushing magnitude of the four -- the value that bounds a future row-13 AC budget from above. Each swept point is a fresh 120 ns transient started from RING0 forced low with `uic` (the ring's DC equilibrium is the unstable all-stages-at-midrail point), the first 60 ns discarded as startup. Step (50p) and settle (60n) match sim/vco's exactly, so the same steady-state frequency is measured the same way and the two campaigns' shared (corner, temperature, supply, VCTRL) rows are directly comparable as an independent reproduction; tran_stop is 120 ns rather than sim/vco's 200 ns, halving the per-transient cost at no measurement cost (the 60 ns retained window still holds 13+ cycles at the slowest point measured here, versus the 4 edges min_edges requires) -- a record states the cross-check against sim/vco explicitly rather than asserting comparability. The reducer's threshold tracks each point's OWN supply (0.5 * VDD, sim/harness/measure.py), which is load-bearing here in a way it is not for a fixed-rail sweep: a threshold pinned to the nominal rail would fold a supply-dependent measurement artefact straight into the reported %/V. timeout_s is 7200 rather than sim/vco's 3600 because this grid is meant to be run with sim/run_corners.py -j on a shared host, where per-point wall clock stretches with contention. process_corners is the ratified rows 19/20 PVT grid (spec/target-spec.md, DR-003, #77).
analysis: transient per swept VCTRL value (`tran 50p 120n uic`, four fixed VCTRL values, one ngspice invocation per PVT point; the supply axis is the corner runner's, one PVT point per supply)
